html:
The Rustamids were a dynasty of Ibadi imams who ruled a state from Tahert, near today's Tiaret in western Algeria, from 777 to 909.

Its founder, Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam, was of Persian origin. Ibadism, with its idea of an elected and accountable leader, appealed to Berbers who resented the Arab governors of the Abbasid caliphs. Tahert became a trading city on routes to the Sahara, known for its scholars and its tolerance of Christians and other Muslims.

The Fatimids destroyed it in 909. Its people fled south to Ouargla and later to the oases of the M'zab, where their descendants still live.
sum: The Rustamids were a dynasty of Ibadi imams who ruled a state from Tahert, near today's Tiaret in western Algeria, from 777 to 909.
